title: Backend and provenance
text: core graph constructor accepts neighbour list, example needs GPU optional clustering package. graph$source_device describes neighbour input. contrast, cuda_provenance(graph) describes current graph_assembly stage: uses CPU Matrix backend. plain list earlier stage-level provenance, graph$source_provenance NULL.
code: library(cudagraphR)  vertex_names <- paste0("cell_", 1:6) index <- matrix(   c(     2, 3,     1, 3,     1, 2,     5, 6,     4, 6,     4, 5   ),   nrow = 6,   byrow = TRUE,   dimnames = list(vertex_names, c("neighbor_1", "neighbor_2")) ) distance <- matrix(   rep(c(1, 1.25), 6),   nrow = 6,   byrow = TRUE,   dimnames = dimnames(index) ) neighbors <- list(   index = index,   distance = distance,   device = "cpu" )  graph <- cuda_knn_graph(   neighbors,   weighting = "gaussian",   symmetrize = "mutual" )  graph #> <cuda_graph vertices=6 edges=6 weighting=gaussian source_device=cpu compute=cpu backend=Matrix> graph$source_device #> [1] "cpu" graph$compute_device #> [1] "cpu" cuda_provenance(graph) #> <cuda_provenance schema=cudaverse-stage/1 stages=1 compute=cpu> #>           stage requested_device device backend   selection_reason fallback #>  graph_assembly        fixed-cpu    cpu  Matrix algorithm_cpu_only    FALSE #>  output_device #>            cpu

title: Backend and provenance
text: cudalearnr installed, cuda_knn result supplies distance neighbour-selection stages. cuda_knn_graph() retains stages separately graph assembly. two provenance objects answer different questions: graph_from_knn$source_provenance explains upstream distance neighbour-selection work; cuda_provenance(graph_from_knn) explains graph assembly performed now.
code: if (requireNamespace("cudalearnr", quietly = TRUE)) {   set.seed(1)   observations <- matrix(rnorm(24 * 4), 24, 4)   rownames(observations) <- paste0("observation_", seq_len(nrow(observations)))    neighbors_cpu <- cudalearnr::cuda_knn(     observations,     k = 3,     batch_size = 8,     device = "cpu"   )   graph_from_knn <- cuda_knn_graph(neighbors_cpu)    graph_from_knn$source_device   graph_from_knn$source_provenance   cuda_provenance(graph_from_knn) } #> <cuda_provenance schema=cudaverse-stage/1 stages=1 compute=cpu> #>           stage requested_device device backend   selection_reason fallback #>  graph_assembly        fixed-cpu    cpu  Matrix algorithm_cpu_only    FALSE #>  output_device #>            cpu

title: Backend and provenance
text: Louvain Leiden use optional igraph package. preserve graph assembly record source provenance, current community_detection stage always CPU. cuda_communities result: source_device still identifies original neighbour source; source_provenance graph-assembly stage; upstream_provenance retains provenance supplied neighbour result; cuda_provenance(communities) reports current CPU igraph stage. Changing source device make graph assembly, Louvain, Leiden GPU-native.
code: if (requireNamespace("igraph", quietly = TRUE)) {   communities <- cuda_louvain(graph)    communities$membership   communities$source_device   communities$source_provenance   cuda_provenance(communities) } #> <cuda_provenance schema=cudaverse-stage/1 stages=1 compute=cpu> #>                stage requested_device device backend   selection_reason #>  community_detection        fixed-cpu    cpu  igraph algorithm_cpu_only #>  fallback output_device #>     FALSE           cpu

what: Optional CUDA source and the hardware gate
title: Backend and provenance
text: following block runs CUDA-enabled R torch runtime cudalearnr available. requires CUDA explicitly rather using device = "auto", verifies CUDA neighbour computation followed fixed-CPU graph assembly. cudaverse NVIDIA workflow sets CUDAVERSE_REQUIRE_CUDA=true. gate, missing CUDA hardware missing integration dependency error, skipped test. Use device = "cuda" CUDA execution requirement. Use device = "auto" recorded CPU fallback acceptable.
code: require_cuda <- identical(   tolower(Sys.getenv("CUDAVERSE_REQUIRE_CUDA", "false")),   "true" ) cuda_ready <- cudatensr::cuda_available() knn_ready <- requireNamespace("cudalearnr", quietly = TRUE)  if (require_cuda && (!cuda_ready || !knn_ready)) {   stop(     "The hardware gate requires CUDA and the cudalearnr integration."   ) }  if (cuda_ready && knn_ready) {   set.seed(2)   cuda_input <- matrix(rnorm(32 * 4), 32, 4)   rownames(cuda_input) <- paste0("cuda_observation_", seq_len(nrow(cuda_input)))    neighbors_cuda <- cudalearnr::cuda_knn(     cuda_input,     k = 3,     batch_size = 8,     device = "cuda"   )   graph_cuda <- cuda_knn_graph(neighbors_cuda)   graph_cuda_provenance <- cuda_provenance(graph_cuda)    stopifnot(     identical(graph_cuda$source_device, "cuda"),     identical(graph_cuda$compute_device, "cpu"),     identical(graph_cuda_provenance$stage, "graph_assembly"),     identical(graph_cuda_provenance$device, "cpu")   )    graph_cuda$source_provenance   graph_cuda_provenance    if (requireNamespace("igraph", quietly = TRUE)) {     communities_cuda_source <- cuda_louvain(graph_cuda)     stopifnot(       identical(communities_cuda_source$compute_device, "cpu"),       identical(         cuda_provenance(communities_cuda_source)$device,         "cpu"       )     )   } }

title: cudagraphR 0.2.0
text: cuda_provenance() now re-exports canonical cudatensr S3 generic instead wrapping , methods registered cudaverse packages remain available regardless package attachment order. Graph assembly community detection now expose shared stage-level provenance schema explicitly report CPU computation independently upstream CUDA kNN source. Graphs retain kNN source provenance; community results retain graph upstream provenance. Gaussian graphs record effective bandwidth chosen sigma = NULL, Leiden results record effective n_iterations. Compatible neighbour lists now validate optional device metadata.
